newsitem.title: USA: Whitman seeks second term as N.J. governor.
newsitem.headline: Whitman seeks second term as N.J. governor.

text.p: Gov. Christine Whitman formally declared Monday she will seek re-election to New Jersey's top job.

The nationally prominent Republican, whose name was often mentioned last year as a possible running mate to presidential candidate Bob Dole, made the announcement during the first of 10 stops she planned in a two-day bus tour of the state.
In 1993, Whitman defeated Democrat Gov. Jim Florio, largely on a pledge to roll back taxes. Since then, she cut the state income tax by 30 percent for most residents.
Bue she declared Monday she has more work to do. "There are more challenges left to meet, and I am asking for another term to meet them," she said.
A lively race was shaping up among New Jersey Democrats, who will hold a primary election June 3.

Last week, three Democrats annnounced their candidacies, each taking the opportunity to criticize the governor. They were state Sen. James McGreevey, who also is mayor of Woodbridge; Michael Murphy, former prosecutor of Morris County, and Robert Andrews, a congressman from Camden County.

All three said Whitman had relied too much on borrowing and accused her of using fiscal gimmicks to balance the budget. They also blamed her for failing to address rising auto insurance rates in New Jersey.

A poll released last week by Quinnipiac College in Hamden, Conn., showed Whitman's approval rating fell to 52 percent from 62 percent in February, in part because of skepticism about her handling of the state budget and taxes.

On the issue of taxes, the poll said Whitman had a negative rating of 42 to 54 percent, down from a positive rating of 49 to 46 percent in February. Pollsters said part of the decline on the tax issue resulted from opposition to Whitman's proposal to borrow nearly $3 billion to pay off debts run up by the state's pension system.
